name: security-mcp-client-registration-trust-review
intent: MCP OAuth registration profiles and client-metadata-to-consent binding
artifacts: MCP authorization metadata, client registration, redirect policy, user consent records and token issuer.
trace: Trace a client identity/redirect through registration to granted resource authority, including reuse of client metadata across protected MCP resources.
experiment: In the chosen registration profile, retain registered metadata and consent transaction for two owned clients. Compare legitimate creation/update with a changed redirect or metadata provenance and inspect the client identity receiving the resulting grant.
disproof: Dynamic registration can be intentional; a client ID alone grants no user/resource permission.
repair: Bind registration and consent to the intended client/resource and preserve legitimate compatible clients.
branch_decisions: Distinguish registration metadata from user consent and from authorization-server identity. Dynamic registration can be a supported public-client flow. Pin the redirect/client relationship and broker transaction so an attacker client cannot reuse another client consent; a new valid client record by itself is not a successful impersonation or token disclosure.
operational_method: Identify the actual registration profile first: pre-registered clients, dynamic registration or supported client-metadata documents are different trust paths. Retain client metadata provenance, redirect selection and the exact client identity displayed/recorded at consent. Compare a legitimate client update with an untrusted metadata/redirect change; open registration alone is expected under some profiles. Generic wrong-resource token validation remains the MCP authorization workflow.
